history.value: Y Combinator was founded in March 2005 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Morris and Trevor Blackwell, and ran its first Summer Founders Program that year. The batch model — a fixed cheque, a fixed programme and a Demo Day — was the innovation, and it moved to Mountain View, California soon after. Sam Altman was president 2014-2019, Geoff Ralston 2019-2022 and Garry Tan from January 2023. YC Continuity, the growth fund, launched in October 2015 and was wound back in March 2023 when YC scaled off late-stage investing. YC now runs four batches a year (from 2025) and states it has funded over 5,000 companies since 2005; its public directory listed 6,203 launched companies when this base was built.

investment_concept.basis: Derived from YC's own description of the standard deal and the batch programme.

sources.source: YC's deal page

investment_concept.value: YC invests a fixed amount in every company it accepts, on identical terms, and runs them through a three-month programme ending in Demo Day. It is an accelerator rather than a stage investor: selection and volume do the work that diligence and cheque-sizing do elsewhere.

investment_stage.basis: Published as ONE label rather than padding the array: the batch investment is the entry for every member, and the calibration gate scored the batch rule 31/31 on the golden set. Pre-Seed and Series A are structurally empty for this investor — YC's own sustained language calls the batch cheque seed funding, and Continuity's mandate was pro rata and later-stage growth, so it never led a Series A. The only non-Seed entries in the entire base are the two ycc_only rows (Convoy, Monzo), which are Growth.

sources.source: YC about page, archived 2009-2020: 'Y Combinator provides seed funding for startups.'

investment_geo.basis: From the landed base's own hq_country distribution: US 76.9% of 6,348 placed rows, then GB 3.7%, IN 3.5%, CA 2.5%. Only the US clears any reasonable core threshold, so the two-label geo cap is not reached and no taxonomy escalation arises — the risk this run's issue flagged did not materialise. 359 of the US rows are flagged country_prior at low confidence (no location evidence on the row) and are excluded from any claim stronger than the ordering.

sources.source: Landed base hq_country distribution, this run

investment_range.basis: NOT a range in the sense the other firms use, and recorded as the fixed instrument it is: YC invests $500,000 per company — $125,000 for 7% on a post-money SAFE plus $375,000 on an uncapped SAFE with an MFN — identically for every company it accepts, so lower, median and upper are the same number. The Form D entry-round median that the other profiles compute is meaningless for an accelerator and is deliberately NOT computed. Historical progression, all from YC's own posts: ~$6,000 per founder (2005-06), $5,000 + $5,000 per founder (2007-09), $11,000 + $3,000 per founder plus an outside note (2010-14), $120,000 for 7% (Apr 2014), $150,000 for 7% (from W19), $125,000 for 7% (from W21), and the $500,000 structure from Jan 2022. YC Continuity separately wrote growth cheques up to ~$144M (Monzo's Series F), but that vehicle was wound back in 2023 and its cheques are not the firm's current instrument.

aum.basis: Y Combinator Management, LLC is an EXEMPT REPORTING ADVISER (CRD 171730, SEC file 802-80528, ERA-active with the SEC since 2014-10-23), not an RIA. An ERA files no Item 5.F regulatory AUM, so both ends of the range are the sworn Section 7.B(1) composite: 19 private funds at $21,962,163,829 total current gross asset value, from the annual amendment filed 2026-03-27. There is no separate YC Continuity adviser registration — Continuity Fund I is reported under this same ADV.

funds.basis: All 19 private funds reported in Section 7.B(1) of the ADV, with their sworn gross asset values. Vintages are null: the ADV does not carry them and Form D is not a reliable substitute here — YC's vehicles file 'Indefinite' offerings. FOUR of these funds appear in the ADV and NOWHERE in EDGAR (Y Combinator Fund I and II, YCVC Fund I, YCVC W14), so a Form D sweep alone would have missed them. Conversely the batch vehicles file real numbers: Y Combinator ES24, LLC sold $152,698,436 and ES26 sold $228,321,282, which is better than the accelerator structure was assumed to support.
